text:
Evidence supports testing objectives before adding architecture. [gSASRec’s IJCAI 2024 summary](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes SASRec weaknesses to overconfidence under sampled BCE; its original 2023 study recommends gBCE calibration t=0.75 and 128–256 negatives, subject to compute limits. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721), approximates full cross-entropy using GPU-efficient maximum-inner-product selection, reporting competitive quality with substantially lower peak memory. [RecSys 2025’s LogQ study implementation](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) supplies controlled SASRec variants covering uniform, in-batch, mixed-negative and corrected sampled-softmax objectives. These findings motivate objective ablations; they do not establish gains on the four Amazon categories.

Hardness alone cannot establish that an unobserved item is a true negative. Earlier [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) explicitly models suspected false negatives using teacher soft labels and consistency regularization, illustrating the risk of aggressively penalizing plausible interests, although teacher training adds cost. Practical inference for this budget: retain SASRec and compare multi-negative sampled softmax against calibrated gBCE first, using vectorized scoring and modest negative counts before scaling. Then test a small mixture of uniform and semi-hard negatives, with warm-up, capped hardness weights, and exclusion of known training positives; these are proposed controls, not proven false-negative identification. Higher Electronics/CDs training ranking error motivates these experiments but does not demonstrate a validation deficit. Select using the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10 and compare GPU time as well as accuracy.
